findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup added inside the creation loop uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") instead of the alias actually created ("idp-alias-" + i). The same mistake occurs at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". As a result, the identity providers created by this test are not removed by the registered cleanup, which can leave stale providers in the test realm and affect other tests. The cleanup should capture and use the generated alias.

findings.title: Null and empty-string organizationId share the same cache search key
findings.body: getForLogin uses `organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` as the search key. A call with `organizationId == null` and a call with an empty-string `organizationId` therefore collide in the cache, even though the delegate query treats empty string as a non-null organization filter and can return a different result. Once one variant is cached, the other may return stale or incorrect providers. A distinct sentinel for null, or a key that preserves the null/non-null distinction, would avoid this. For FetchMode.REALM_ONLY, organizationId is ignored by the query, so keying by it also creates unnecessary cache entries.

findings.title: getForLogin does not consider organization invalidation for organization-specific results
findings.body: getForLogin can cache organization-specific results under the same per-mode cache key, but it only bypasses the cache when the login cache key itself is invalid. Unlike getByOrganization, which also checks `isInvalid(orgId)`, this method does not check whether the supplied organizationId has been invalidated. If an organization is removed or invalidated without an IDP create/update/remove also invalidating the login cache key, a stale organization-specific login list may be served. Consider bypassing the cache when `organizationId != null && isInvalid(organizationId)` or ensuring all organization changes invalidate these login keys.

findings.title: Login cache entry per FetchMode can accumulate unbounded organization search keys
findings.body: For each realm and FetchMode, getForLogin stores all organization-specific results in a single IdentityProviderListQuery, using the organizationId as a search key inside that entry. In realms with many organizations, this single cache entry can grow without bound and is rewritten whenever a new organizationId is queried (see the invalidate/merge path around lines 234-241). This can cause memory pressure and cache churn. A per-organization cache key or some bound/eviction strategy would be more scalable.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException in remove() for unknown alias when cache key is invalid
findings.body: remove(alias) fetches `storedIdp` from the delegate, which is null if the alias does not exist. If `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true, the code calls `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which dereferences the model and will throw a NullPointerException. remove() should safely return false for unknown aliases; guard against a null storedIdp before invalidating, or make registerIDPInvalidation null-safe.
